paper.title: Resolving catastrophic error bursts from cosmic rays in large arrays of superconducting qubits
paper.observable: repeated excited-state preparation, 1 us wait, and binary relaxation readout (RReCS)

model_scope.calibration: population and observation-layer distributions use MAIN calibration recordings; QP coefficients were not fitted to Google QP measurements
model_scope.test_use: test recordings were excluded from QP tuning, but had been inspected during earlier profile development
model_scope.implementation_relation: the toolkit and companion experiment use the same simulator calculation core; packaging and default-layout imports differ

fast_leave_one_event_out.warning: 15 evaluations are three unique events repeated across five simulation seeds; candidate ranges were informed by prior inspection of these events

fast_posterior_predictive.warning: simulation ranges were calibrated after inspecting the same three real events; this is not independent validation

main_spatial_zero_shot.channel_mapping_assumption: zero-based MAIN channel 26 is treated as the undocumented extra channel

conclusion: The Google-calibrated model has moderate temporal consistency with recording-separated MAIN events and tentative FAST wavefront support, but it does not outperform the empirical temporal backend and its zero-shot spatial transfer is weak. This is not evidence of cross-device generalization or microscopic radiation-transport accuracy.
